title: Hosted residency control plane: tenant anchor assertions & automated compliance archive
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Objective: Build a control-plane feature for Hosted API that lets tenants declare region commitments (anchor assertions), set per-tenant retention profiles, and produce tamper-evident evidence bundles automatically. The feature should enable downstream audit exports and short-circuit common compliance review requests with signed snapshots of placement + retention decisions.

Why now: Increasing enterprise adoption has led to frequent manual evidence requests and ad-hoc scripts to prove data residency. Customers want a single workflow to declare residency requirements, have the platform enforce them on routing, and receive periodic attestations they can push to internal auditors.

Scope:
- UI flow for tenants to declare a primary region and soft/hard region preferences (soft affinity, strict lock, fallback region).
- API model for pinned-region declaration + retention policy (TTL, retention-class mapping).
- Control-plane enforcement that influences request routing decisions and emits immutable decision records.
- Evidence composer that compiles routing decisions, retention profile snapshots, config hashes, and delivery logs into an attestable archive (zip + signed manifest).
- Scheduled snapshot job and ad-hoc export endpoint for compliance teams.

Out of scope: cross-cloud host guarantees, on-prem private deployments (handled in separate Private project), long-term archival storage service (we export to customer-owned buckets).

Success metrics:
- Reduce average manual evidence request turnaround time from 3 business days to <2 hours for 90% of requests.
- 95% automated export success rate for scheduled snapshots across pilot tenants.
- No increase in routed request latencies > 10ms p95 attributable to residency enforcement.

Non-functional constraints and tradeoffs considered:
- Signing and attestation: HSM integration provides strong guarantees but increases delivery complexity. For initial rollout we'll use platform KMS signing with rotation and append a KMS-key identifier to evidence manifests.
- Enforcement strictness: Strict locks can lead to request rejects during cross-region outages. Design will include a configurable fallback policy with alerting and optional soft-fail mode for early adopters.
- Evidence size: Full request logs are large; evidence composer will include compact decision traces and pointers to full logs stored in the tenant's retention bucket to keep bundles manageable.

Deliverables:
- PRD and UI mockups linked below.
- OpenAPI: residency declaration endpoints (+ examples).
- Control-plane routing hook and decision logging implementation (ENG work).
- Evidence composer microservice and scheduled snapshot worker.
- Acceptance tests and a compliance wizard in Console to fetch & validate exported bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant can create/modify a residency declaration via Console and API
Routing decisions record region chosen and policy applied for each request
Scheduled evidence export generates signed bundle containing manifest, policy snapshot, and compact decision traces
Ad-hoc evidence export endpoint returns downloadable attestable archive within SLA
Console shows retention profile and last export timestamp per tenant
